input.claim_text: On 3 February 2023 heavy rain caused the creek behind our property to overflow and water came into our home, ruining the carpets in the living room and soaking the bottom of the plasterboard walls. It happened really fast, within about an hour the water was ankle deep inside. We've had to rip up the carpet already because it started smelling. I think it'll cost around $9,000 to fix the flooring and walls.

output.cause: creek overflowed due to heavy rain
output.damaged_item: living room carpets and plasterboard walls

Based on the provided excerpts, here is the information on Flood cover and its definition/exclusions:

## Flood Definition

The excerpts provide a partial definition of "Flood" through its exclusions:

- Flood **excludes** water from Actions of the Sea, **except** when caused by:
  - a Storm Surge, if it occurs at the same time your Insured Property is damaged by a Storm; or
  - a Tsunami
- Flood also **excludes** a mixture of water from Actions of the Sea and water from any other source [RAA Contents PDS, page 88]

Note: The excerpts do not contain a complete standalone definition of "Flood" itself (e.g., specifying it relates to the escape/overflow of water from watercourses, lakes, etc.). Only the exclusionary boundaries of the definition are shown above.

## Flood Cover Exclusions

Under the "12. Flood" section, cover does **not** apply to loss or damage:

- to any part of the Home that is not fully built
- to tennis courts
- to a wharf, jetty, pontoon or sea wall
- to water in a tank, swimming pool or spa, including the cost of cleaning mud or debris out of a tank, swimming pool or spa
- to swimming pools or spas and their covers or liners, **except** for permanently attached hard lid style pool covers
- to paint, when there is no structural damage caused by a Flood to other parts of the Home
- caused by underground (hydrostatic) water
- to a glasshouse or greenhouse
- to unsealed paths or driveways, such as gravel or constructed with any loose materials
- caused by Flood which arises from deliberate or Malicious Damage to, or destruction of, a reservoir or dam
- to a path or driveway (and other listed items) if they were **not** structurally sound or **not** maintained in a reasonable manner prior to the loss or damage occurring (this list is cut off in the excerpt and may include additional items beyond "a path" and "a driveway")

[RAA Contents PDS, page 50]

## Additional Relevant Details

- Flood cover applies to both Building and Contents, up to the **Applicable Sum Insured**, and is subject to a **72-hour waiting period** [RAA Contents PDS, page 34].

input.query: flood cover for building and contents combined home policy

turns.text:
DECISION: approve

Reasoning: The claim involves damage to carpets and plasterboard walls caused by a nearby creek overflowing after heavy rain — this is a classic "Flood" peril (rainfall runoff/watercourse overflow), which is an explicitly listed Insured Event under the RAA policy [RAA Contents PDS, page 50]. None of the listed flood exclusions apply here — there's no damage to unbuilt structures, tennis courts, wharves, pools/spas, paint-only damage, underground hydrostatic water, or unsealed paths/driveways [RAA Contents PDS, page 50], [RAA Contents PDS, page 88]. The damage described (carpet and lower wall plasterboard soaked by rising floodwater) is consistent with covered flood damage, not an excluded cause.

Policyholder-specific figures were retrieved from the RAA certificate of insurance: excess = $500, coverage limit = $45,000. Applying these to the estimated claim amount of $9,000:

Payout = $9,000 − $500 excess = **$8,500**, which is well within the $45,000 coverage limit.

Sources cited:
- [RAA Contents PDS, page 50]
- [RAA Contents PDS, page 88]
- [RAA Contents PDS, page 34]

Note: The PDS mentions a 72-hour waiting period for flood cover, but no evidence indicates the policy was newly incepted or that this claim falls within such a window, so this is not a basis for denial without further contradicting information.
